newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on holiday.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on holiday.

text.p: Most Shanghai copper futures contracts ended slightly down on Wednesday on profit-taking ahead of the four-day Labour Day holiday, traders said.
The exchange will be closed from Thursday to Sunday with trading resuming next Monday.
The most actively traded August 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 23,600 yuan ($2,845) per tonne, losing 50 yuan. It opened at 23,650 and hit a high of 23,700 yuan per tonne.
May fell 90 to 23,460, June 10 to 23,600 and July 40 to 23,600 yuan per tonne.
September was unchanged at 23,580 and October fell 100 to 23,500 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 27,190 tonnes from 45,490 tonnes.
Copper opened mixed and profit-taking ahead of the holiday pushed prices down with most contracts closing at or near their intraday lows, traders said.
Traders said many investors were not willing to hold long positions before the long break.
"Many investors liquidated their long positions because of the holiday," one trader said.
Traders said copper was likely to have a technical rebound when the market re-opened on Monday.
"Technical charts are in favour of mid-term long position holders," a second trader said.
Physical prices are around 23,500 yuan per tonne in the Shanghai area, traders said.
Aluminium ended up. May rose 60 to 15,580, June 150 to 15,900 and July 10 to 16,090 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 280 tonnes from 730 tonnes.
